key_insight: MOJO combines masked autoencoding self-supervision with supervised spike decoding, enabling neural population models to use unlabelled data and generalize better in low-label settings.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more data-efficient training recipe for brain-computer interfaces and closed-loop neural systems, especially when labeled recordings are scarce or expensive to obtain.
method: Spike-tokenizing model pretrained with masked autoencoding on unlabelled neural data
Joint optimization of self-supervised and supervised decoding objectives
Applied across spiking datasets and extended to human ECoG speech decoding
evidence_signal: Across three spiking datasets and human ECoG speech recordings, MOJO outperformed purely supervised models, with the biggest gains in few-shot finetuning and label-limited training.
watch_item: Benefits depend on access to substantial unlabelled neural data and may require careful adaptation when transferring across species, tasks, and recording modalities.
paper_title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
